label: Corning ADSS 36F aerial, G.652.D
notes: Corning 036ELE-T3322A20 product spec sheet (Corning Optical Communications ecatalog, revision date 2026-11-28): “Aerial Dielectric Self-Supporting Cable, ADSS 36 F, Single-mode (OS2), A-D2Y(T)2Y, (3 x 12)”. Three active loose tubes of 12 in twelve tube positions with nine filling elements, dielectric central element, dry core held by swellable elements, non-metallic strength members over the core, black polyethylene jacket, halogen-free; 15.1 mm nominal diameter, 161 kg/km, crush 3000 N/10 cm, max tensile 1700 N long-term / 4000 N short-term, min bend radius 265 mm installation / 225 mm operation, -5 to +50 C installation and -40 to +70 C operating and storage, Telcordia tube and fibre colour code, ITU-T G.652.D / IEC 60793-2-50 B1.3 fibre, cable cutoff 1260 nm, mode-field diameter 9.2 um at 1310 nm and 10.4 um at 1550 nm, dispersion <= 18 ps/(nm km) at 1550 nm and <= 22 at 1625 nm, PMD link design value <= 0.06 ps/sqrt(km). Why the row exists: the aerial family shipped 12/24/48 (gh#147), then 72 for the 49-72 band and 96/144 (gh#173), and cableFor answers with the SMALLEST cable that fits, so a 25-36 fibre pole span was bought as 48F. Measured on this engine, a ladder of the aerial rungs plus the duct and drop rungs a plant still needs answers design.cableForSpan(32, 1200, ladder, registry) with g652d-adss-48; 32 strands is a 32-drop splitter site or a 16-house active tree at two strands a house - an ordinary village or MDU distribution run - and 36F is 4 spare fibres instead of 16. The figures are the 24F and 48F rows’ figures because the build is the same 12-position stranded core with one active tube per 12 fibres (1 x 12 at 12F, 2 x 12 at 24F, 3 x 12 here, 4 x 12 at 48F), and the count is the vendor’s, not a rung invented to even the ladder: the part number in sourceUrl resolves to this sheet. Attenuation, and exactly what kind of figure it is: the sheet publishes MAXIMA only, 0.36 dB/km at 1310 nm, 0.36 at 1383 nm and 0.22 at 1550 nm, and no 1490 nm figure at all. This row carries 0.35 / 0.22 / 0.21, the same typical installed row g652d-adss-12, -24 and -48 carry, so an aerial span is budgeted on the same footing as its duct neighbours; 1490 nm is interpolated between the two published windows and is not a citation from Corning or ITU-T. Corning’s 0.36 at 1310 nm sits 0.01 dB/km above the 0.35 here: hold the supplier to 0.36 in acceptance and read the as-built OTDR before signing. drumM is deliberately absent, the family decision the 12/24/48/72 rows record: the sheet prints “Max. cable length per reel/drum 6000 m” in its Dimensions block, a ceiling rather than a put-up, and declaring it bills a 6 km reel for a short aerial spur - measured on engine/length.js for the sibling rows, 0.7 km of route buys 6,000 m at a 6000 m drum against 2,000 m at the engine default, and 12 km buys 18,000 against 14,000, the two agreeing only between 4.8 and 6 km. With no drumM the engine falls back to engine/length.js’s 2,000 m and the BOM row carries 2,000 m with no field saying whether that is a drum or the engine default, so enter the reel actually ordered. What is not modelled, and worth knowing before it bites: CABLE_USES has no “aerial” value, so nothing in the planner knows this cable hangs from poles - the tags and this note carry it - and no span, sag, ice or wind loading check exists, so a design will run the row over any span drawn and the pole-to-pole distance stays the planner’s decision; nothing metallic means nothing to bond or earth at a joint. Tie-break trap: cableFor answers with the SMALLEST cable that fits and breaks equal fibre counts on model id, and g652d-adss-* sorts before g652d-loose-*, so a ladder naming both an aerial and a duct rung at the same count buys the aerial one - name the row actually stocked, not both. This row is not in DEFAULT_LADDER (no aerial row is), so the part alone re-ranks nothing: it reaches a design through the design ladder option, or an engine change to the default. One product spec sheet’s figures, not a measured build: replace with the cable actually purchased and its as-built attenuation before ordering.
